messages:
maria: Hey @eng-runtime — incoming escalation from a customer (ticket #CS-9142). They see p95/p99 latency regressions on hosted API after yesterday's model rollout. p50 ~ stable, p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~420ms, p99 hits ~1.1s on short prompts. They provided these request ids: rq_8a3f, rq_8a52, rq_8b10. They say it started ~2026-03-11 22:30 UTC. Can someone triage? :eyes:

jason: Thanks — pinging here. Do we know which model variant was rolled? Any quantization profile changes in the rollout?

maria: Deploy notes mention "enable int8_autotune for redwood-3B-v2" and a quant profile bump. Deploy-bot attached the rollout id: rollout_20260311_340. Also saw a calibration job with a warning in the deployment log: `calib_job warning: 3.7% activations out of range` but apparently the job finished.

deploy-bot: rollout_20260311_340 completed: redwood-3B-v2 -> quant_profile=v2-int8-autotune (flag: int8_autotune=true).

tina: Quick hypothesis: if calibration produced some out-of-range activations, kernel selection might have chosen a safe fallback kernel path that uses extra memory copies or serialized launches. That can increase tail latency even if mean looks ok. Do we have the perf traces?

maria: Attached to the ticket: small perf snippet from customer (they ran their normal smoke tests):
```
p50: 180ms
p95: 420ms  (prev 210ms)
p99: 1100ms (prev 320ms)
throughput: ~unchanged
seq_len distribution: mostly short (<128), occasional ~512 prompts
```

jason: Can you paste the model config from the node that served rq_8a3f? Also, is KV cache status the same? Sometimes int8 kernels require a different KV layout and we degrade to no-kv-cache which spikes p95 for repeated chat calls.

maria: From node logs (snip):
```
[2026-03-11T22:28:03Z] model=redwood-3B-v2 config: quant_profile=v2-int8-autotune, quant_force_fp16=false, int8_fallback=false
[2026-03-11T22:28:03Z] calib: completed (warnings: activations_out_of_range=3.7%)
[2026-03-11T22:28:03Z] runtime: using safe-kernel-path for attn, KV-cache=enabled
[2026-03-11T22:28:04Z] runtime: kernel launches increased by 1.5x vs fp16 baseline
```

linda: Interesting — safe-kernel-path but KV-cache=enabled suggests we didn't disable cache, good. But extra kernel launches + different kernel shapes can still add tail latency. Could also be memory bandwidth contention if int8 kernels increase host<->device copies for calibration metadata. Any host metrics?

jason: I can repro locally. Running a short loadtest with the same model + quant_profile shows p95 regression when prompts occasionally hit ~512 tokens (even though most are short). My quick profiler shows extra memcpy before each chunk: looks like int8 tiled copy into aligned buffers.

tina: That matches: int8 autotune chooses tiling/packing for small per-head dims; if the packing path isn't vectorized well for short sequences, we lose latency on p95 endpoints. Also if calibration flagged activations out-of-range, we might have disabled some fused kernels and fallen back to unfused safe path.

maria: Customer is asking for mitigation now — what can we propose short-term?

jason: Immediate mitigations:
- Roll back quant_profile for that model to previous known-good (v2-fp16) on hosted until we fix autotune.
- Or set `quant_force_fp16=true` on that variant (non-destructive).
- Route that customer's org to fp16 variant (pinning in routing rules) — quick and minimal blast radius.

linda: Operational hotfix: I can run the following to flip the flag on the node pool serving their org: (one-liner)
```
redwoodctl patch serving-node --selector=pool=hosted-us-east --set "models.redwood-3B-v2.quant_force_fp16=true"
```
I'll do a canary (10%) first and watch p95 for 5m.

maria: Please do that ASAP. Customer is sensitive (paying dedicated usage next month).

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 "p95 regression after int8_autotune rollout" (severity: P2).

jason: Also adding a short-term runtime toggle to re-enable int8_fallback=true so kernels that fail calibration go back to fp16 paths automatically. That avoids manual rollbacks when calib warnings > threshold. I'll open PR and patch a canary.

tina: Long-term action items I propose:
- Add stricter calibration gating: if activations_out_of_range > 1% then fail autotune and keep fp16.
- Record calibration artifacts (sample inputs + activation histograms) to S3 for offline analysis and retraining of quant params.
- Add microbench suite for short-seq tails (mix of 90% <128, 10% around 512) in CI to detect p95 wins/losses before rollout.

maria: Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate after fix. Suggested repro curl they can run: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model": "redwood-3B-v2", "prompt": "<pad to 512 tokens>", "max_tokens": 64}'
```
They should run 1000 requests with a mix of short and a few long prompts and check p95/p99.

jason: Quick note: if you want to run a local reproduce script I used: 
```
python perf_test.py --model redwood-3B-v2 --quant-profile v2-int8-autotune --prompt-mix short:90,long:10 --concurrency 8 --requests 2000
```
This reproduces the tail for me.

linda: Canary patch applied to 10% pool. Monitoring dashboards: p95 dropped ~40% for canary nodes within 3m after applying `quant_force_fp16=true`. Keeping watch for 15m before sweeping.

maria: Nice. Customer updated: "Thanks, we saw improvement when routed to fp16 — please keep us posted for permanent fix." :thumbsup:

jason: I'll open two PRs: (1) runtime: enforce fallback when calib_warnings>1% (exception: allow override flag for experiments), (2) deploy tooling: add pre-rollout perf-smoke for tail cases. I'll link both PRs here when open.

tina: I'll capture the calibration artifacts for rollout_20260311_340 and push to s3://redwood-calib/artifacts/rollout_20260311_340 so model team can inspect.

maria: Ops-bot, can you tag the ticket with "quantization" and link the incident?

ops-bot: Ticket CS-9142 updated: labels=[quantization, latency, customer-impact], incident=INC-2026-042.

linda: After 15m the canary is stable, p95 on canary nodes is back to baseline. I'm rolling the patch to 100% over 10m.

maria: Thanks team. Next steps for customer comms: 1) tell them we rolled a temporary fix (forced fp16 for their route), 2) explain root cause = aggressive int8-autotune + calibration warnings -> safe-kernel fallback increasing kernel launches and tail latency, 3) next update when autotune gating + perf-smoke PRs merged.

jason: PRs created: runtime#482 (autotune gating), deploy#210 (pre-rollout perf-smoke). Linking when CI passes.

tina: Uploaded calibration artifacts and a short analysis: unusual spike in activation histogram for head 7 layer 10 — suggests calibration dataset mismatch. Details: s3://redwood-calib/artifacts/rollout_20260311_340/analysis.txt

maria: Closing the thread for now — incident remains open until PRs merge. I'll update customer and set expectation for permanent fix timeline (2 weeks). Thanks all. :heart
